## Personality

Loud, warm and practical; she runs her boat and her family the same way, with a lot of shouting and a lot of love.

## Lore

Sorcha is thirty-eight, the loudest voice in the Fishers' Coves and the owner of the best catch of any boat in Goa Harbour. She runs her boat and her family the same way, with a lot of shouting and a lot of love, and most people in the coves have been on the receiving end of both. She is warm, practical and impossible to ignore. When Sorcha laughs on the water, they say, the gulls go quiet to listen.

### Born in the coves

Sorcha is the daughter of Agna, the net-mender, who has kept the coves' nets whole for fifty years. Her father, Donal, was a cove fisher, a big, slow-spoken man who taught her to handle a boat before she could swim properly. He died of a winter fever fifteen years ago, and his boat, the Sea Thrift, came to Sorcha. She has fished from it ever since, and she will not hear a word about replacing it, though it has been patched so often that her mother says there is more mending in it than boat.

Agna and Sorcha are very alike, which is why they argue. Agna has an opinion about everyone's knots, Sorcha's included, and Sorcha has an opinion about everything else. They see each other every day and would be lost without it.

### Calder and the children

Sorcha married Calder thirteen years ago. She says she chose him because he was the only man in the coves who could be shouted at without shouting back; he says he simply waited until she noticed him. He is the calm half of the best boat in the coves: she finds the fish, he mends whatever broke finding them, and between them they bring in more than anyone. She teases him endlessly about his dream of building a bigger boat and racing it around Veligor, and quietly puts aside a little of every good catch toward it.

They have two children. Eilidh, ten, is bossy, clever and already guts a fish faster than most grown-ups, and Sorcha sees so much of herself in her that it sometimes frightens her. Ronan, seven, is dreamy and forever wandering off after shells and feathers, and Sorcha spends half her evenings shouting his name along the shore.

### The rougher sea

For most of Sorcha's life, the children came out on the Sea Thrift as soon as they could sit still, and went wherever the fish were. These last few years the sea has turned rougher, and the weather beyond the point has become hard to trust. Her mother finds nets torn by something with teeth far bigger than any fish she knows. Sorcha has stopped taking Eilidh and Ronan out past the point at all. Eilidh is furious about it. Sorcha has not explained, because she is not sure what she would say.

### The market and the favour

Sorcha sells most of her catch to Brodie, the fishmonger at the Lantern Market, whose smoked fish goes out on ships all over Veligor. Two winters ago she let him have a whole season's catch on credit when his smokehouse roof fell in, and he swore he would repay the favour. He keeps forgetting. She keeps reminding him, loudly, in front of customers, and secretly enjoys it more than any repayment.

### What she wants

Sorcha wants her children to inherit a sea they can fish safely, and she wants Calder to have his boat. She fears the day the coves cannot feed themselves from the water, and the night one of her own does not come home.

### Hooks

A quest might help Sorcha find out what is tearing her mother's nets beyond the point, or finally collect Brodie's favour. She would also pay well, in fish, for anyone who could keep Ronan in sight for a whole afternoon.
